chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, and Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, altogether from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to me: 'O Jabir! Is it sufficient for the one who claims Shia-ism that he says he loves us, the People of the Household? By Allah, our Shia are only those who fear Allah and obey Him. And they, O Jabir, were not recognized except by humility, reverence, trustworthiness, frequent remembrance of Allah, fasting, prayer, righteousness towards parents, attending to the poor, the destitute, the indebted, and the orphans, truthfulness in speech, recitation of the Quran, restraining their tongues from people except for good, and being trusted by their clans in matters.'

Jabir said: 'So I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We do not recognize anyone today with this description.' He said: 'O Jabir! Do not let the sects carry you away. It is enough for a man to say, 'I love Ali and follow his Wilayah,' yet not be a doer of that. If he were to say, 'I love the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),' and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is better than Ali (peace be upon him), yet he does not follow his way and does not act by his Sunnah, his love for him would not benefit him at all.'

So fear Allah and work for what is with Allah. There is no kinship between Allah and anyone. The most beloved of servants to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the most honored by Him, is the most pious of them and the most active in His obedience. O Jabir! By Allah, one does not draw near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, except through obedience. And we do not have exemption from the Fire, nor is there a proof for anyone against Allah. Whoever is obedient to Allah is a friend to us, and whoever is disobedient to Allah is an enemy to us. And our Wilayah is not attained except through deeds and piety.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the true characteristics of a Shia according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) critiques the superficiality of 'verbal Shia-ism' by defining true allegiance through tangible piety (Taqwa) and ethical conduct, such as humility and trustworthiness. He establishes that Wilayah is not an automatic entitlement of lineage but a spiritual station attained through obedience to Allah, reinforcing the Shia principle that love must be validated by action. This narrative serves as a critical counter to tribalistic or nominalist interpretations of Shiism, grounding identity in moral and ritual practice.
